Precursor

/pri-KUR-ser/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Precursor means something that came before and led to the development of another thing; a forerunner.

The abacus was a precursor to the modern calculator, working out sums centuries before electronics existed.

Worked Example

Film historians treat the silent newsreel as a precursor to today's televised evening news.

The silent newsreel came first AND directly shaped what followed — that two-part relationship (earlier + led to the later thing) is exactly what makes something a precursor, not merely something old.

How Precursor Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

forerunner

forerunner: something that came before and signaled what was to follow

predecessor

predecessor: the thing that held a place or role before the current one

antecedent

antecedent: an earlier thing from which a later thing developed

Antonyms

successor

successor: the thing that comes after and takes over

descendant

descendant: something that developed later, out of an earlier source

How Strong Is It? — predecessor → precursor → progenitor

predecessor vs. precursor

predecessor vs. precursor: Predecessor is weaker — it only says something held the spot earlier, with no claim that it shaped what came next; a precursor actively led to the later development.

progenitor vs. precursor

progenitor vs. precursor: Progenitor is stronger — it names the direct source or originator from which something descends, while a precursor merely ran ahead and paved the way.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of precursor.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — pre-

Prefix — pre-: before, in advance (Latin prae-)

Root — curs

Root — curs: to run (Latin currere, past stem curs-)

Suffix — -or

Suffix — -or: one that does (agent noun ending)

Put it together

Put it together: Pre- ('before') + curs ('to run') + -or ('one that does') builds 'one that runs ahead.' A precursor literally runs out in front of what follows, clearing the path for it.

Use the root in a new word: excursion

Use the root in a new word: excursion: The class took an excursion to the aquarium — literally a 'running out' from school for the day.

Root Check

Word Choice

Academic / historical

Precursor usually appears in writing about the history of science, technology, music, or ideas, and is typically followed by 'to' or 'of' ('a precursor to the internet'). It always points FORWARD from the earlier thing — never call the later invention a precursor of the earlier one.
